claims.text: Take w/ meals and a glass of H2O; ⍉ on an empty stomach (potential for gastric irritate).
claims.quote: Potassium chloride extended release tablets should be taken with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid. This product should not be taken on an empty stomach because of its potential for gastric irritation

claims.text: Potassium chloride ER (KCl) safety: CI: hyperkalemia (further ↑ serum K can prod ♡ arrest).
claims.quote: Potassium supplements are contraindicated in patients with hyperkalemia since a further increase in serum potassium concentration in such patients can produce cardiac arrest.

claims.text: CI: any struct, pathological, or pharm cause for arrest or delay in tablet passage thru the GI tract.
claims.quote: All solid oral dosage forms of potassium chloride are contraindicated in any patient in whom there is structural, pathological (e.g., diabetic gastroparesis), or pharmacologic (use of anticholinergic agents or other agents with anticholinergic properties at sufficient doses to exert anticholinergic effects) cause for arrest or delay in tablet passage through the gastrointestinal tract.

claims.text: In pts w/ impaired K excretion, potassium salts can prod hyperkalemia and ♡ arrest; potentially fatal hyperkalemia can develop rapidly and be aSx.
claims.quote: In patients with impaired mechanisms for excreting potassium, the administration of potassium salts can produce hyperkalemia and cardiac arrest. This occurs most commonly in patients given potassium by the intravenous route but may also occur in patients given potassium orally. Potentially fatal hyperkalemia can develop rapidly and be asymptomatic.

claims.text: ⍉ tx hypokalemia w/ concomitant potassium salts and a potassium-sparing diuretic (ex, spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride): severe hyperkalemia.
claims.quote: Hypokalemia should not be treated by the concomitant administration of potassium salts and a potassium-sparing diuretic (e.g., spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride) since the simultaneous administration of these agents can produce severe hyperkalemia.

claims.text: Closely monitor K w/ concomitant RAAS therapy (ACEis, ARBs, spironolactone, eplerenone, or aliskiren).
claims.quote: Drugs that inhibit the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) including angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), spironolactone, eplerenone, or aliskiren produce potassium retention by inhibiting aldosterone production. Closely monitor potassium in patients receiving concomitant RAAS therapy.

claims.text: Closely monitor K w/ concomitant NSAID therapy.
claims.quote: Closely monitor potassium in patients receiving concomitant NSAID therapy

claims.text: D/c STAT and consider ulceration, obstruct, or perf if severe vomiting, abd pain, distention, or GI bleed occurs.
claims.quote: Potassium chloride extended release tablets should be discontinued immediately and the possibility of ulceration, obstruction, or perforation should be considered if severe vomiting, abdominal pain, distention, or gastrointestinal bleeding occurs.

claims.text: Careful monitoring of serum K and appropriate dosage adj required in chronic renal dz or any condition impairing K excretion.
claims.quote: The use of potassium salts in patients with chronic renal disease, or any other condition which impairs potassium excretion, requires particularly careful monitoring of the serum potassium concentration and appropriate dosage adjustment.

claims.text: OD: hyperkalemia = USU aSx and may be manifested only by an ↑ serum K (6.5 to 8 mEq/L) and ECG chgs (peaking T-waves, loss of P-waves, S-T depression, QT prolongation).
claims.quote: hyperkalemia is usually asymptomatic and may be manifested only by an increased serum potassium concentration (6.5 to 8 mEq/L) and characteristic electrocardiographic changes (peaking of T-waves, loss of P-waves, depression of S-T segment, and prolongation of the QT-interval)

claims.text: OD tx: IV calcium gluconate if the pt = @ ⍉risk or ↓risk of developing digitalis toxicity.
claims.quote: Intravenous calcium gluconate if the patient is at no risk or low risk of developing digitalis toxicity.
